FACULTY SENATE OFFICE 224 P ASTORE H ALL , 51 L OWER C OLLEGE R OAD , K INGSTON , R I 02881 U SA , P: 401.874.2616 Faculty Senate Resolution 2025-2026-01 Resolution of Appreciation and Gratitude Honoring Kent and Diane Fannon WHEREAS , Kent and Diane Fannon, distinguished alumni of the University of Rhode Island, Class of 1974, have made a profound and lasting impact on the University through their longtime support of the University of Rhode Island; and WHEREAS , the Fannon’s previous gifts, including direct scholarships for students, endowed support for the College of Business, and establishment of the Diane and Kent Fannon Education Research Endowment, have already made a significant impact on the University and its students; and WHEREAS , the University College for Academic Success has evolved into a dynamic center for student community and support under the visionary leadership of founding Dean Emerita Jayne Richmond and current Executive Director Kim Stack; and WHEREAS , the Fannon’s commitment to student achievement, career readiness, and holistic support have now propelled the launch of the Fannon Institute for Student Success, which will transform the University College for Academic Success with revitalized and modernized programming; and WHEREAS , the new Fannon Institute for Student Success will bring together, under one administrative umbrella, five key areas of student support: Career and Experiential Education, Academic Enhancement, Retention, Exploratory Advising, and Student-Athlete Support Services; and WHEREAS , creation of the Fannon Institute for Student Success will transform the student experience, ensuring that every student has access to the tools, mentorship, and resources to succeed; and, finally, WHEREAS , Kent and Diane Fannon’s extraordinary generosity is a testament to their unwavering belief in the power of education and their desire to leave a legacy that will inspire future generations; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED , that the Faculty Senate of the University of Rhode Island, on behalf of the entire General Faculty, expresses its profound appreciation and heartfelt gratitude to the Fannon Family for their visionary generosity, their enduring legacy of support for URI students, and their commitment to ensuring that generations of students will have the tools and resources they need to achieve their highest ambitions; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED , that this resolution be entered into the official minutes of the Faculty Senate and that a copy be sent to Kent and Diane Fannon as a token of our deep appreciation.

Unanimously adopted this Twentieth day of November in the year Two Thousand and Twenty-Five. ________________________________________ _________________________________________ Travis D.

Existing Language: 6.10.10 Policy Statement on Freedom of Expression.
Faith in the fundamental importance of freedom forms a major theme in the history, government and tradition of the State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations and of the United States of America.
Freedom is also recognized on practical grounds as vital to scholars in their search for and dissemination of truth.
Although academic freedom is not written into law, it is well established in custom and grounded in traditions of long standing in the colleges and universities of the Western world, protecting professional scholars and teachers from interference with their obligation to pursue truth.

Though it is a specific kind of freedom peculiar to members of the teaching profession in higher education, its benefits ultimately accrue as much to the public at large as to the scholars themselves.
In fact, the present age of accelerating change emphasizes that education must stress development of the capacity for critical thought, a capacity that can be achieved only when freedom in inquiry and discussion prevail.

COURSES CASC Bill 25-26-05A At the February 5, 2026 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART406 | Advanced Studio Seminar II, effective Fall 2026 (2 crs.) This senior capstone course builds on Advanced Studio Seminar I. Students will finish their art portfolio and prepare to professionally exhibit it while further developing their professional skills. (Studio) Pre: ART405. Not for graduate credit CHM221 | Organic Chemistry I Workshop, effective Fall 2026 (1 cr.) This course is a companion course to CHM227 where students will get more discussion regarding common topics in organic chemistry, such as mechanisms, acid -base chemistry, and organic structures. (Lec. 1) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in CHM227. May be repeated for a maximum of 2 credits. SMC100 | Multimedia Toolbox for Sports Media, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Students learn the basics of multimedia competencies, including the Adobe Creative Suite and other programs to produce quality and ethical sports content. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: SMC majors only. SMC101 | The Sports Media Industry, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Students will analyze sports media professions, industries and technologies in relation to their histories all the way up to key trends. (Lec. 3/Online) SMC201 | Sports Audiences and Fandom, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) What does it mean to be a fan? This course explores psychological and sociological theories behind fandom, while paying attention to how media professionals target and reach fans. (Lec. 3) Pre: SMC100 and SMC101.

CSC161 (DSP161) | AI for Everyone, effective Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Cross-listed as (CSC) DSP161.
Introduces Artificial Intelligence (AI) to students from all disciplines, demystifies AI, and explains the fundamental concepts of AI.
Explores AI tools that can enhance academic performance and overall college experience. (Lec. 1) COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: EVE476 | Environmental Engineering Processes, effective Spring 2027 (2 crs.) Fundamentals of physical and chemical processes used in environmental engineering for the treatment of water, soil, air, and hazardous wastes. (Lec. 1, Lab. 1) Pre: CVE374 and CVE375, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
MCE457 | Aerodynamics, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Explores how air flows around bodies and how lift, drag, and aerodynamic forces are generated, including airfoils, wings, viscosity effects, and basic wind-tunnel measurements. (Lec. 3) Pre: MCE354, completed or concurrently enrolled in MCE414, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
INTERDISCIPLINARY NEUROSCIENCE PROGRAM: NEU487 (PSY487) | Seminar for Undergraduate Teaching Assistants, effective Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Cross-listed as (NEU) PSY487.

Students will learn pedagogies and engage in activities designed to enhance teaching skills. (Seminar) Pre: junior or senior standing, and permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

Project-based assignments promote creative thinking and problem solving using industry-standard tools to critically engage with contemporary design issues. (Studio) ART214 | Photography I: Seeing like a Camera, effective Fall 2026 Change title, credits, description (4 crs.) Introduces basic photography and editing, including analog processes with a focus on digital photography.
Emphasizes photography as an artistic medium.
It includes required projects, lab work, readings, and discussions. (Studio)

ART215 | Video and Multimedia I, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, repeat status (4 crs.) Introduction to video production, editing, and web distribution, with an emphasis on experimental video, video art, and video installation.
Required studio projects and readings. (Studio) ART231 | Print Media I: Analog and Digital Printing, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, title, remove prerequisites (4 crs.) Introduction to printmaking and digital printing through the processes of relief and various digital printing processes. (Studio) ART344 | Sculpture II: Contemporary Sculptural Practice, effective Fall 2026 Change title, credits, repeat status (4 crs.) Continuation of ART243. (Studio) Pre: ART243 or permission of instructor.
May be repeated for up to 8 credits with permission of instructor, doing increasingly independent work.
ART405 | Advanced Studio Seminar I, effective Fall 2026 Change title, description, credits, repeat for credit status, prerequisites (2 crs.) This senior capstone course guides students in creating a unified portfolio of their work and developing the professional skills needed to succeed. (Studio) Pre: Art BA (by permission) or Art BFA major, senior standing.

Not for graduate credit.
SPA325 | Introduction to Literary Genres, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Presentation of the novel, poetry, drama, and essay as literary genres.
Textual commentary and methods of criticism. (Lec. 3) Pre: SPA206 or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: AVS412 | Animal Nutrition, effective Summer 2026 Add online modality to existing in-person course (3 crs.) Principles of animal nutrition, metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats; mineral and vitamin requirements; nutritive requirements for maintenance, growth, reproduction, lactation, and work. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: junior standing or above.
Not for graduate credit.

BIO302 | Animal Development, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) (Lec. 3) Pre: BIO260 or BIO360 or BIO272
